name: sec-audit10-viewer-event-filtering
title: Security audit item 10 (F9), MCP0a: sensitivity tags on log lines and role-filtered PollEvents: viewers/editors no longer get audit, rate-limit or peer lines or host absolute paths
issue: Security audit item 10 / finding F9 of C:/Method Notes Obsidian/orchestrator/proposals/editor-host-security-audit-2026-10-15.md (read F9 and the recommended-order table row 10 first) and C:/Method Notes Obsidian/orchestrator/proposals/mcp-engine-design.md section on MCP0 (the reason it is a prerequisite: AI agents and shared hosts must not see other users' names, peer IPs and host paths). The user accepted ALL recommendations on 2026-10-20 (MCP0 before agents are pointed at shared hosts). TODAY: PollEvents returns the whole process log (users, roles, peer IPs, rate-limit lines, absolute paths) to every authenticated role including viewers. SCOPE: (1) SENSITIVITY TAGS on log records: extend the logger/EventRing record (find editor-server's event ring and the engine Logger hook that feeds it) with a sensitivity level (e.g. Public | Operator | Admin) assigned at the call site or by category: the audit: lines, 'Rate limit:' lines, peer=/address lines, token/identity/user lines, pre-auth/busy/takeover lines and anything that prints an absolute host path are Admin (or Operator) only; engine/game logs the project's scripts and components produce (Lua print/Debug.Log, component warnings) stay visible to every role. Prefer explicit tagging at the call sites you can find (grep Logger:: calls in editor-server/ and the audit/rate-limit/pre-auth code paths) with a safe default for untagged lines (decide: untagged engine lines are Public; untagged editor-server lines are Admin: justify and test); NEVER filter by string matching alone. (2) PollEvents (and any other command or event that returns log lines: grep for the log/event ring consumers, GetEngineHealth, the audio/health events) filters by the caller's role: admin sees everything; editor and viewer see only Public lines; a --no-token loopback host (no roles) keeps today's full visibility for the single local user (state this and test it); the ring must keep its eviction behaviour and sequence numbers consistent per client (a client must not see sequence gaps that leak the existence of hidden lines: either number per role view or document that gaps can occur: choose the safer one, test it). (3) REMOVE absolute host paths from anything non-admin roles still receive in events (paths in public lines become res://-relative or are stripped): coordinate with item 11 (error responses) only by keeping this item to the LOG/EVENT surface. (4) TESTS: PollEventsTests per role (admin full; editor and viewer filtered; no-token loopback full), a golden list of the exact audit/rate-limit/peer line prefixes being Admin-only, untagged-default behaviour, path stripping, sequence behaviour, concurrency of the ring unchanged; no protocol change (allowProtocol false: if the fix needs a protocol change STOP and report in needsUser). (5) DOCS: docs/logging-and-editor.html (what each role sees in the event stream: verify against the code), docs/editor.html roles text, docs/testing.html. Verify every docs sentence against the CODE. Nothing builds locally; CI (10 checks) is the test; expect fix rounds.
acceptance: Log records carry a sensitivity tag; audit, rate-limit, peer, identity and host-path lines are admin-only; script/component logs stay public
PollEvents (and other log-returning surfaces) filter by the caller role; no-token loopback keeps full visibility; no sequence leak of hidden lines
Per-role tests and a golden list of admin-only prefixes; no protocol change
All 10 checks green; docs verified against code
notes: Reviewer: every audit/rate-limit/peer/identity/path log site is tagged (grep all Logger calls in editor-server), nothing sensitive reaches editor/viewer through ANY other surface (health, events, errors), default for untagged lines is safe, sequence handling leaks nothing, no-token loopback behaviour documented and tested, docs true, mediums count.
